name: IUCN NL Land Acquisition Fund

funder.name: IUCN National Committee of the Netherlands (IUCN NL)

summary: Fund for locally registered conservation NGOs and civil society organisations in Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Pacific to buy or lease land and set up other area-based protection that secures habitat for threatened species. Grant size is set in the applicant guidelines.

geography.label: Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Pacific

eligibility.rule: Locally registered as a non-profit NGO or CSO in an eligible region
Directly responsible for preparing and implementing the grant project
Have a qualifying organisational bank account
Have proven conservation-area management experience and capacity
Not an individual, commercial/government organisation, or project in agriculture, education, rescue or rehabilitation

documents: Map(s) of the project area within the wider landscape

status.quote: The deadline for applications is Friday, 1 May, 2026.

deadline.quote: The deadline for applications is Friday, 1 May, 2026.

applicant_types.quote: be locally registered as a non-profit organisation, non-governmental organisation (NGOs) or civil society organisation (CSOs) in Africa, Asia, Latin America, or the Pacific

geography.quote: be locally registered as a non-profit organisation, non-governmental organisation (NGOs) or civil society organisation (CSOs) in Africa, Asia, Latin America, or the Pacific

access.quote: The IUCN NL Land Acquisition Fund calls on local conservation NGOs and CSOs worldwide to submit proposals to acquire threatened nature, create safe reserves, and connect habitats for endangered species.

window.quote: The deadline for applications is Friday, 1 May, 2026.

eligibility.quote: be locally registered as a non-profit organisation, non-governmental organisation (NGOs) or civil society organisation (CSOs) in Africa, Asia, Latin America, or the Pacific
be directly responsible for the preparation and implementation of the grant project
have a bank account in the name of the organisation and in the place where the organisation is established or where the project is carried out
have proven experience and capacity in managing conservation areas, including project management, financial management, and financial control

private individuals; commercial (for profit) organisations; governmental institutions; and projects or organisations with a primary focus on sustainable agricultural systems, education, rescue, or rehabilitation centres

documents.quote: Map(s) of the project area - map(s) should also show the project area within the wider landscape and highlight any other areas that enjoy some form of (legal) protection, indigenous territories, community lands, or sustainably certified forestry concessions

effort.quote: The deadline for applications is Friday, 1 May, 2026.
a limited number of applicants will be invited to submit a full proposal.

steps: Pre-proposal of up to 4 pages, by email
